author: reek
body: A Codex-on-Codex install: drive 0 is a boot stick carrying a FAT16 ESP with EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI, CODEX.CDX and SOURCE.SRC on it, drive 1 is blank, and the guest partitions, formats and installs onto drive 1 without leaving Codex.

author: reek
body: This could not be attempted before 2026-07-27: block-select selected nothing, every drive position was the same disk, and the install would have partitioned and formatted the disk it was reading from.

author: reek
body: The reading is a digest of each file on each side, not merely that it arrived. The two reads go through different filesystems on different drives -- FAT16 on the source, FAT32 on the target this program just created -- so equal digests over equal lengths mean the bytes crossed intact rather than that one reader agrees with itself. Lengths alone would pass on files of zeros.

author: reek
body: All three files are checked because a stick that boots and cannot verify or rebuild itself is not the promise. The boot image alone is what the install used to copy.
